scope: Theorem 1.3 (Quasilinear PCP for PPAD) of the manuscript “The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction” (preprints/The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinear-reduction-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 136 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a7ab4d86183890be), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are fixed rational constants 0 < ε < 1 10, 0 < δ < 1, a fixed positive integer A, a fixed nonnegative integer b, a fixed polynomial p with nonnegative integer coefficients, and deterministic algorithms R, D with the following properties. (i) Every generalized circuit in Definition 1.2 has an acceptable rational assignment of encoding length at most p(M). (ii) For every End-of-Line instance I of length N, the output R(I) is a generalized circuit whose complete encoding length satisfies M ≤ AN  log2(N + 2) b . (iii) The construction R runs in time polynomial in N, with one fixed polynomial bound. (iv) For every acceptable assignment x of R(I), the algorithm D(I, x) returns a solution of I in time polynomial in N plus the encoding length of x, with one fixed polynomial bound. All constants, polynomials, and algorithms are chosen once. They use no advice depending on the input length and no randomized construction.
